title: bug: claim_next_task's file-collision notice doesn't mark which colliding peers are live and mentions nobody, so two live seats editing one file learn of it only at landing
description:
Observed twice on 2026-10-30, both times on docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

1. 03:43:45Z: the collision notice for task-915d7e84 listed bc8410af among 8 peers. bc8410af's completion landing (03:44Z) held docs/MCP_SERVER.md as MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-915d7e84). QA then rejected bc8410af at 03:50Z because its docs never reached HEAD.
2. 06:16:18Z: the collision notice for task-574c0b36 listed the live CQ-V03 (task-9cc13170, worker-e60b90bd, started 06:14Z) among 5 peers. 574c0b36's landing e67ca0e (06:22:35Z) committed V03's in-progress MCP_SERVER.md hunks under 574c0b36's id. Nothing was lost, but both workers and both QA reviews had to untangle the attribution by hand.

Root cause: claimNextTask.ts (about line 741) builds the notice from util/affectedFiles.ts computeFileCollisions. That function treats every nonterminal row that declares the file alike: a peer that is assigned and actively being edited looks the same as an unassigned row that is still waiting on its dependencies. It then posts to #workers with no @mentions. chat_wait only wakes a seat on a mention or a human message, so nobody is paged. The claim response's fileCollision array carries the same undifferentiated list.

Wanted: flag the colliding peers that are live (assigned to a registered, non-DEAD worker), and page those seats plus the claimer, so they can coordinate before either one lands. Keep it advisory: the claim is never blocked.
definitionOfDone: Each claim_next_task response fileCollision entry whose peer task is assigned to a registered, non-DEAD worker carries that worker's id (for example liveAssignee). Entries for unassigned peers, or peers held by a DEAD seat, carry none. Unit tests cover all three cases.

When at least one colliding peer is live, the #workers notice @mentions each live peer's assignee and the claiming worker, so their chat_wait wakes, and lists the live peers before the dormant ones. A claim whose only collisions are dormant posts no mention. Tests assert the message's mentions in both cases.
The claim is never blocked or delayed by collision computation (a failure is still swallowed), and the docs/MCP_SERVER.md claim_next_task section describes the new field.

implementationPlan.description:
RED tests first, in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts. Put them next to the existing 'claiming a task with overlapping files returns a fileCollision warning, does not block' test. That test must stay green unchanged: its worker-a is never registered, so it gets no liveAssignee.

Shared fixture: setupMoe('TURBO'); writeEpic(); plus a second epic 'epic-2' written the same way. writeTask task-B: WORKING, unassigned, one plan step with affectedFiles ['src/foo.ts']. WORKING peers, each with a step on 'src/foo.ts':
- task-live: epicId 'epic-2', assigned 'worker-live'. It must be in a different epic: the single-worker-per-epic+status rule (claimNextTask.ts ~605) skips a teamless claimer whose epic+status a live other worker already holds.
- task-unassigned: assignedWorkerId null.
- task-dead: assigned 'worker-dead'.
- task-gone: assigned 'worker-gone', which is never registered.
Then `await state.load()`. After load, register with state.createWorker: 'worker-live' (status 'CODING', currentTaskId 'task-live', epicId 'epic-2') and 'worker-dead' (status 'DEAD'). Claim with `claimNextTaskTool(state).handler({ workerId: 'worker-b', statuses: ['WORKING'], taskId: 'task-B' }, state)`. Capture chat with `state.subscribe(e => ...)`, keeping MESSAGE_CREATED events (payload is the message, `routingTargets` the routed seats). Unsubscribe in finally.

Cases:
(a) DoD 1, liveness: `fileCollision` toEqual exactly, sorted by task id as today: task-dead, task-gone, task-live, task-unassigned. Each has files ['src/foo.ts']. Only task-live carries `liveAssignee: 'worker-live'`. The other three must have no liveAssignee key at all. This covers unassigned, DEAD-held and unregistered-held.
(b) DoD 2, live notice: exactly one MESSAGE_CREATED event whose payload.content contains 'file collision on task-B'. Its payload.mentions toEqual ['worker-live', 'worker-b']. Its routingTargets toEqual ['worker-live', 'worker-b']: those are exactly the seats whose chat_wait wakes (chatWait.ts isRelevant). 'task-live' appears before each dormant id in the content. 'worker-dead' and 'worker-gone' never appear in it.
(c) DoD 2, dormant-only: the same fixture without task-live and worker-live. task-B and task-unassigned both also list 'packages/@scope/x.ts'. Then payload.mentions toEqual [] and the content still names task-unassigned, task-dead and task-gone. RED today: the raw '@scope' in a path parses as a mention (mentionRouter.ts parseRawMentions).
(d) DoD 3, a failure is swallowed: after load, corrupt one peer in memory so the scan throws: `(state.tasks.get('task-unassigned')!.implementationPlan[0] as unknown as { affectedFiles: unknown }).affectedFiles = 42;` (collectTaskAffectedFiles then throws 'not iterable'). The claim resolves with hasNext true and no `fileCollision` key, and state.getTask('task-B').assignedWorkerId is 'worker-b'. RED today: computeFileCollisions runs outside any try, so the tool throws AFTER the assignment and attempt were written. If something earlier in the claim path trips on the corrupt peer instead, find an injection that only the collision scan reaches, and say so in the step note.
(e) Mention safety: a live peer whose registered assignee id is not one mention token, e.g. 'worker x' (in its own epic). The response entry still carries liveAssignee 'worker x'. The notice's payload.mentions toEqual ['worker-b'] and routingTargets toEqual ['worker-b']. Unfiltered, '@worker x' at line start would parse as the group token 'worker' and page every worker seat.

Run `npx vitest run src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts` and record the RED output. (a), (b), (d) and (e) fail; (c) fails on '@scope'. The suite's other tests pass. From WSL, run it in the Linux-native snapshot described in step 4.
implementationPlan.note: RED (Linux-native snapshot /tmp/moe-4d67-gate.hM9aKi, env -i, node v24.21.0): `npx vitest run src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts` → Tests 5 failed | 14 passed (19). (a) fileCollision lacks liveAssignee; (b) mentions [] not ['worker-live','worker-b']; (c) mentions ['scope'] not [] (raw '@scope' in a path parses as a mention); (d) 'TypeError: number 42 is not iterable' thrown from computeFileCollisions at claimNextTask.ts:741, after the assignment was written; (e) liveAssignee undefined. The pre-existing collision test stays green. Deviation from plan (e): state.createWorker validates ids ([A-Za-z0-9_-] via validateEntityId), so 'worker x' cannot be registered through the API; the fixture creates the worker with a safe id and re-keys the in-memory record to 'worker x', standing in for a hand-edited workers/*.json. (d) injection (affectedFiles=42) is reached only by the collision scan, as planned. Shared tree: claimNextTask.ts and governanceFeatures.test.ts had no foreign dirty hunks before my edit.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts, in the collision block at ~734-752 (the response spread at ~835 needs no change). claimNextTask.ts is also declared by the dormant WORKING row task-af83018e (CQ-V09). Edit it only with a wrapper-observed editing tool, so the skip-untouched landing takes it; a shell write leaves no witness and it would be held as MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED.

1. Liveness. `let fileCollision: Array<FileCollision & { liveAssignee?: string }> = [];` Import the FileCollision type from ../util/affectedFiles.js; leave affectedFiles.ts itself untouched. Inside `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.warn({ error, taskId: task.id }, '...'); fileCollision = []; }` (logger is already imported), map computeFileCollisions' result. For each entry, look up the peer with state.tasks.get(c.task). When `peer?.assignedWorkerId && !state.isTaskAssignedToInactiveWorker(peer)`, return `{ ...c, liveAssignee: peer.assignedWorkerId }`; otherwise return c untouched, with no key. This is the claim path's own claimability predicate: missing or DEAD means inactive. It never looks at idle time, because a quiet seat is still live (workerStore.ts isTaskAssignedToInactiveWorker). Keep the response array's existing task-id order.

2. Notice, still in its own try/catch and still awaited (one bounded append, as today).
- describe(c) = `${c.task}: ` followed by the first 3 files, each wrapped in an inline code span (backtick, file, backtick), joined by ', ', plus '…' when there are more. Code spans are blanked by stripQuotedSpans, so an '@' inside a path is never a mention.
- live = entries with liveAssignee; dormant = the rest.
- No live entry: post exactly `⚠️ file collision on ${task.id}: ${dormant.map(describe).join(' | ')}`. That is today's wording, with no mention.
- Otherwise: page = the unique ids of [...live assignees in order, params.workerId when set], filtered with /^\w[\w-]*$/ (the token grammar of parseRawMentions in util/mentionRouter.ts). An id that cannot round-trip as one mention, say one with spaces or newlines, is never written with '@', so it cannot smuggle in a group token. Content: `${page.map(id => '@' + id).join(' ')} ⚠️ file collision on ${task.id}. Live: ${live.map(describe).join(' | ')}`, then `; dormant: ${dormant.map(describe).join(' | ')}` when there are dormant entries, then `. Coordinate before either of you lands.` Do not print assignee ids anywhere else in the content; the structured liveAssignee carries the mapping for the claimer.
- Update the block comment above to match: advisory, never blocks the claim, live peers paged.

The error handling and edge cases are tested in step 1:
- A computation failure leaves fileCollision [] (no key in the response) and logs a warning.
- A post failure is swallowed as today, and postToRoleChannel also catches internally.
- No workerId: page only the live assignees.
- A claimer that is also a live assignee is deduped.
- A live assignee that equals the claimer's id cannot happen in practice; dedupe covers it anyway.
Re-run `npx vitest run src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts src/util/affectedFiles.test.ts` until all pass.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN in the snapshot: `npx vitest run src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts src/util/affectedFiles.test.ts` → 2 files, 48 tests passed. claimNextTask.ts: added markLivePeers (state.isTaskAssignedToInactiveWorker predicate, no idle heuristic), describeCollision (code-quoted files, first 3, backtick swapped for a quote), collisionNotice (live first; page = unique live assignees + claimer filtered by /^\w[\w-]*$/; dormant-only keeps today's wording with no mention), and wrapped the computation in try/catch with logger.warn. Added one test beyond the plan, (f): a path containing a backtick would end its code span early and could page a seat; covered by the quote swap. Edits went through the Edit tool only (wrapper-observed). git diff of claimNextTask.ts showed only my hunks.

Post in #workers mentioning that task's assignee so they know the hunks will ride this completion commit, and name the carried hunks in the completion summary so QA can attribute them. That is the hand-untangling this task exists to prevent.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
(a) The claim still never fails or waits on collisions. Every new line sits inside a try, the computation is synchronous over in-memory maps under the claim mutex, and nothing new does IO except the existing awaited post.
(b) Liveness matches the claimability predicate exactly: missing or DEAD means dormant; quiet-but-registered means live. No idle-time heuristic.
(c) A seat that dies between the computation and the post gets one stale advisory mention, which is harmless.
(d) No raw id is written with '@' unless it is a single mention token, and nothing else in the content can form a mention: task ids are daemon-generated and paths are code-quoted.
(e) The dormant-only wording is unchanged apart from the code-quoted files.
(f) The response stays additive: liveAssignee is optional, there is no key on dormant entries, and the order is unchanged. The existing collision test and affectedFiles.test.ts stay green.
(g) The 10 KB chat cap: a giant collision list makes the post fail, which is logged and the claim is unaffected (unchanged behaviour).
(h) Re-check `git diff` for the three contested files right before complete_task, as in step 3. No .moe edits, no forbidden patterns.
Fix anything found, re-run the step 4 gate if any byte changed, then complete_task with the step 4 evidence and the step 1 RED output.
implementationPlan.note: Self-review of the task's own diff (claimNextTask.ts, governanceFeatures.test.ts, docs/MCP_SERVER.md). planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Chosen: compute liveAssignee in claimNextTask.ts with the existing state.isTaskAssignedToInactiveWorker predicate, and build the notice there. The change stays in one runtime file, and util/affectedFiles.ts stays a pure file-overlap util. 2) Rejected: passing workers into computeFileCollisions. That widens a pure util's signature and its tests for no gain. 3) Rejected: reordering the response array live-first. The DoD only orders the notice, and the response order is an existing contract. 4) Rejected: blocking or delaying the claim on a live collision. The task says advisory only.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Chat mentions are parsed from content: parseRawMentions in util/mentionRouter.ts strips code spans/blocks and matches /(?<![\w@])@(\w[\w-]*)/. Group tokens ('worker', 'workers', 'all'...) address only in a line's addressing prefix. routeSystemMessage routes to the parsed mentions when there are any, otherwise to every non-IDLE, non-DEAD seat. chat_wait wakes when routingTargets includes the seat. The claimer's worker record is created or updated before the collision block (claimNextTask.ts ~664), so its mention resolves. Role channels are ensured on load (persistence.ts ensureRoleChannels). In tests, state.subscribe receives MESSAGE_CREATED with routingTargets. The single-worker-per-epic+status rule (~605) skips a teamless claimer when a live other worker holds the same epic+status, so the live peer in tests needs its own epic.
